historical_record.description: Built as a wedding present from Ephraim Willard Burr, the former mayor, to his son, its construction supervised by the bride's father, Thomas Barnard, a Nantucket builder: a three-storey Italianate house with a Second Empire roof, finished on every side, in a large garden with a cottage behind. Water was turned on on 2 August 1878, and the family kept the house until 1969; the architect has never been confirmed.
The earthquake badly shook the front porch and steps and displaced the moulding above the brick foundation; the porch was rebuilt with its present columns and roof by 1913.

A one-storey Arts and Crafts photography studio, designed by Henry H. Gutterson, was built for a daughter of the family on the north side of the property facing Green Street; Gutterson raised it to two storeys in 1937. It has since been split off as a lot of its own.
Designated San Francisco Landmark No. 31. The house was then turned to lawyers' offices before becoming a home again in 1995.
Listed on the National Register of Historic Places as an Italianate house with Second Empire elements and for its large garden, rare in the city.

unknowns: The house is dated 1875 in the city's landmark designation and about 1878 from its water service record.
